findings.title: Pure deletions of default-branch lines are never reported
findings.why: `now` and `before` are built by `_added`, which records only added head-side ranges. A new commit that simply deletes a line from the default branch has no `hunk.added`; the `elif` only fires when the removed lines overlap `before` (lines the PR had previously added). The increment therefore comes back empty even though the author changed the PR by deleting a line. The symmetric case, re-adding a line the PR had previously deleted, is also missed because that line is not an addition against the default branch.

findings.title: Diff path parsing breaks on quoted paths and configurable prefixes
findings.why: `_FILE` assumes an unquoted `diff --git a/PATH b/PATH` header and splits it with greedy groups. Git still C-quotes paths containing tabs, quotes, backslashes, etc., even with `core.quotePath=false`, and `diff.noprefix`/`diff.mnemonicPrefix` can change the `a/`/`b/` prefixes. When the header does not match, lines 48-49 leave `old_path`/`new_path` at the previous file, so subsequent `@@` hunks are attributed to the wrong file. Paths containing ` b/` can also be split at the wrong delimiter. This silently drops or misattributes review lines.

findings.title: Removal fallback can return a line that is not in the head tree
findings.why: `at` is `max(new_start, 1)`. If a removal hunk empties a file or deletes it entirely, `new_start` is 0 and the code records `(1, 1)` for a path that has no line 1, or no file at all, at `head`. `Increment.lines` is documented as head-side lines, so downstream code that anchors comments to `head` can fail or target the wrong location.

findings.title: Diff does not disable textconv filters
findings.why: `git diff` enables textconv by default; `--no-ext-diff` only disables external diff drivers. A PR's `.gitattributes` can still select a configured textconv driver, causing a helper to run on untrusted repository content and making hunk line numbers refer to converted text rather than the real head file. The resulting ranges can then be wrong. Add `--no-textconv`.
